entries.reasonNote: Named in design-scale.md and design-scale-implementation.md as part of the in-flight provider-aware-concurrency migration. Cut 2 (pending) adds `recommendedConcurrency: 20` on the filesystem provider that 'matches existing DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY'; Cut 2's risk note shows `mapLimit(items, fn, DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY)` as the explicit-pass shape callers use until Cut 3 migrates them. Removing the export now would force re-adding it when scale Cut 2-3 lands.

Forward-compat scaffolding for the Cache foundation's `CacheError` taxonomy. design-cache.md Gap 5 defines the base class + `CacheConfigurationError` + `CacheSchemaError` with explicit reasoning ('Throws reserved for unrecoverable infrastructure errors per Universal Provider Requirement #6') and invites plugin authors writing v2 providers (Redis, Azure) to extend the base class. design-cache-implementation.md Cut 8 ships the types pre-Path-X-Phase-3 and lists the pending consumer wiring as 'throw `CacheConfigurationError` on bad config' in memory.ts. The file's own JSDoc states 'Two leaf classes today; more land as v2 providers ship and surface their own failure modes'. Deleting now would force re-creation when Cut 8's wiring lands and would force plugin providers to roll their own error hierarchy.

OCP extension seam for the upload-preprocessor registry. The file's top-of-module JSDoc explicitly enumerates planned future preprocessors that will extend this registry: 'HEIC: transcode to JPEG (browsers can't display HEIC) — future', 'Animated GIF: extract first frame as poster, set `animated` manifest flag — future', 'JPEG with EXIF: apply orientation, strip personal metadata — future'. The export pairs with `runPreprocessors`'s default-parameter pattern (line 111: `preprocessors: readonly UploadPreprocessor[] = defaultPreprocessors`) — that pattern only makes sense as a named exported registry callers can compose against via `[...defaultPreprocessors, customPreprocessor]`. Two consumers (ingest.ts:100, ingest-locale.ts:90) document the `preprocessors?` input field's default behavior by referencing `defaultPreprocessors` by name in JSDoc. The file's SOLID-lenses section explicitly calls out 'OCP: adding a format = new module + register; ingest unchanged' — the registry IS the registration point. Deleting now and re-introducing when the first future preprocessor lands would force JSDoc churn at three locations + re-promotion of the const. Cost of keeping: one named const.

Load-bearing internal helper for a public-API type. `HasEmbeddedBrand<T>` is used at types.ts:409 by the `Content<T>` type mapper, which IS exported as part of the public `gazetta/schema` surface (re-exported from packages/gazetta/src/schema/index.ts:36 and documented as the canonical usage pattern in its top-of-file JSDoc — template authors write `TemplateFunction<Content<z.infer<typeof schema>>>`). Deleting `HasEmbeddedBrand` would break `Content<T>` and the public schema API; tests in packages/gazetta/tests/schema-content.test.ts cover this composition end-to-end across all three branded asset kinds. The type is also part of a deliberately parallel triad with `HasDownloadableBrand` and `HasFontBrand` (declared on adjacent lines with identical structure, sharing one section comment that frames them as 'Brand detection for Content<T>' and explicitly calls out 'If Zod v5 changes brand representation, update only this module'). The trio forms one coherent brand-detection module — splitting one out would break the parallelism that makes future Zod-version migrations a single localized edit. Knip flagged it because no external file imports it directly, but the internal use by an exported type is what makes it load-bearing.

Knip false positive — the type is used at line 411 in the same module, inside the `Content<T>` type mapper (`: HasDownloadableBrand<T> extends true ? ResolvedDownloadableAsset : ...`). Deleting it would break the type-level `Content<T>` cascade and the build. Knip flagged it as 'unused export' because no OTHER file imports it (the type is only used within its declaration file). The proper resolution is a refactor — drop the `export` keyword from all three brand predicates (`HasEmbeddedBrand`, `HasDownloadableBrand`, `HasFontBrand`) so they become file-scoped — but the per-finding prompt says 'this bot deletes; it doesn't redesign,' so refactor is out of scope. The three types form an intentional coherent triple: the file's own comment block at lines 374-389 explicitly calls them out as a group ('If Zod v5 changes brand representation, update only the `Has*Brand` predicates') and they are exported symmetrically. Maintainer judgment is needed on whether to: (a) drop `export` on all three (most likely correct — they're internal to `Content<T>`'s implementation and not re-exported from `schema/index.ts`), (b) leave as-is (cheap, type-level only, no runtime cost), or (c) promote to public API by adding to `schema/index.ts`'s re-export list (if external type authors writing utilities like `IsAssetRef<T>` would benefit). Note: knip flagged only this one of the triple; if knip is configured to nudge toward file-scoping unused exports, then `HasEmbeddedBrand` and `HasFontBrand` should be flagged too — the asymmetry may itself be a knip quirk. None of the three are in `packages/gazetta/package.json`'s `./schema` exports map (verified — `schema/index.ts` re-exports a curated set that excludes the `Has*Brand` predicates).

Knip is technically correct — no source file imports from the `primeicons` npm package — but the dependency encodes clear intent that needs a human design decision before removal. Evidence of intent: (1) `apps/admin/index.html` line 8 loads the PrimeIcons stylesheet via the unpkg CDN: `<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://unpkg.com/primeicons/primeicons.css">`; (2) the admin uses 131 `pi pi-*` PrimeIcons CSS class references across 35 Vue components (e.g. ComponentTree.vue 12, CmsToolbar.vue 11, AuditDrawer.vue 9, plus PreviewPanel/PublishPanel/DevPlayground/TemplateImpactPanel/ActiveTargetIndicator/PurgeBlockedModal each with 6-7). The dep at `^7.0.0` matches the unpkg CDN's served version; removing it loses the version-intent record (and the current CDN URL is unpinned, which is a separate latent issue). The right resolution is a refactor a human should choose: (a) delete the dep AND commit to CDN-only delivery (probably pinning the CDN URL to a version while at it), or (b) drop the unpkg `<link>` from index.html and add `import 'primeicons/primeicons.css'` in the client entry so the icons ship through Vite + the vite-plugin-pwa precache like the rest of the assets — path (b) is more consistent with the existing precache strategy (which currently misses the icon font + CSS). Either path is correct; neither is a 'bot deletes; doesn't redesign' move. Verified no other source references to `primeicons` exist beyond the CDN `<link>` and package.json/package-lock.json (the knip-parse.test.ts hits are test fixtures, not real consumers).
